title: Scheduled report delivery is failing
body: Delivery failures are almost always an expired data source credential or a bounced recipient address. Check the Delivery Log for the specific error before re-running the schedule.

title: Changing a report schedule
body: Edit the schedule under Reports > Delivery. Changes apply from the next run; the current run is not cancelled.

title: Report delivery windows and skipped runs
body: A scheduled report that overruns its window is skipped rather than queued. Consecutive skips raise a warning in the Delivery Log.

title: Timezone handling in scheduled reports
body: Schedules run in the workspace timezone, not the recipient's. Daylight saving transitions shift delivery by an hour unless UTC is selected.

title: Adding recipients to a scheduled report
body: Recipients are managed per schedule. External addresses require the workspace to permit outbound delivery to unverified domains.

title: Report delivery to distribution lists
body: Distribution lists are supported but bounce handling is limited: a single hard bounce disables the whole list until an owner re-enables it.

title: Pausing all scheduled reports
body: An owner can pause delivery workspace-wide under Settings > Delivery. Paused schedules do not accumulate a backlog.

title: Scheduled report shows stale data
body: The report renders against the last completed refresh. If the refresh is running when delivery fires, the previous snapshot is sent.

title: Report subscription limits by plan
body: Business permits 25 active schedules per workspace, Enterprise 250. Disabled schedules do not count.

title: Resending a failed report delivery
body: Use Resend in the Delivery Log. Resending re-renders the report, so the content may differ from the original attempt.

title: Email delivery troubleshooting
body: Check the Delivery Log first. Most failures are recipient-side: full mailboxes, aggressive spam filtering, or a domain that rejects our sending IPs.

title: Verifying a sending domain
body: Add the provided DKIM and SPF records to your DNS. Verification usually completes within an hour but can take up to 48.

title: Why an email landed in spam
body: Unverified sending domains are the most common cause. Verify the domain and ask recipients to mark the first message as not spam.

title: Alert notification channels
body: Alerts can deliver by email, webhook, or in-app. Each channel is configured independently and a failure in one does not suppress the others.

title: Muting alert notifications
body: Alerts can be muted per user or per workspace. Muting suppresses delivery but still records the trigger in the alert history.

title: Alert threshold configuration
body: Thresholds are evaluated on each refresh. An alert that would fire on every refresh is rate limited to one notification per hour.

title: Notification digest settings
body: Digests batch notifications into a single message. Digest frequency is per user, not per workspace.

title: Changing the reply-to address
body: The reply-to address is set per workspace under Settings > Delivery. It does not affect the envelope sender used for authentication.

title: Changing your billing plan
body: Plan changes take effect immediately and are prorated. Downgrades that exceed the new plan's seat limit are blocked until seats are removed.

title: Understanding your invoice
body: Invoices list seat charges, usage overages, and any prorated adjustments from a mid-cycle plan change.

title: Updating a payment method
body: Only billing administrators can update the payment method. The change applies to the next invoice, not to an outstanding one.

title: Failed payment and account suspension
body: After three failed attempts over ten days the workspace becomes read-only. Data is retained and access is restored on payment.

title: Requesting a refund
body: Refunds are available within 14 days of an invoice for unused prorated time. Usage overages are not refundable.

title: Seat counting and inactive users
body: A seat is consumed on invitation acceptance. Deactivating a user frees the seat at the next billing cycle, not immediately.

title: Annual versus monthly billing
body: Annual billing is invoiced up front at a discount. Switching from annual to monthly takes effect at renewal.

title: Tax and VAT details on invoices
body: Add your tax identifier under Settings > Billing. Invoices already issued are not reissued with a new identifier.

title: Usage overage charges
body: Overages are billed at the end of the cycle. A usage alert can be configured to warn before the included allowance is exhausted.

title: Resetting your password
body: Use the Forgot Password link on the sign-in page. The reset link expires after 30 minutes; request a new one rather than reusing an old link.

title: Configuring SAML single sign-on
body: SSO is configured under Settings > Authentication. Meridian supports SP-initiated SAML 2.0. Just-in-time provisioning is optional and off by default.

title: SAML login loops back to the sign-in page
body: A redirect loop almost always means the ACS URL or entity id does not match the identity provider configuration. Compare both exactly.

title: Enabling two-factor authentication
body: 2FA is enforced per workspace under Settings > Authentication. Enforcing it signs out all sessions that have not enrolled.

title: Lost two-factor device
body: An owner can reset a user's 2FA enrolment. Recovery codes issued at enrolment also work and are single use.

title: Session length and idle timeout
body: Sessions last 30 days by default, with an optional idle timeout. Changing either does not terminate existing sessions.

title: SCIM user provisioning
body: SCIM keeps users and groups in sync from your identity provider. Deprovisioning through SCIM deactivates rather than deletes.

title: Login blocked by IP allowlist
body: If an allowlist is configured, sign-in from outside it fails with a generic error rather than naming the allowlist.

title: Service account authentication
body: Service accounts authenticate with a long-lived key and cannot use SSO. Rotate keys under Settings > API.

title: Connecting a Postgres data source
body: Add the connection under Settings > Data Sources. Meridian requires a read-only role and allowlisting of our egress IPs. SSL is required.

title: Connecting a Snowflake warehouse
body: Use a dedicated warehouse and role. Meridian will not create objects; the role needs only USAGE and SELECT.

title: Connecting BigQuery
body: Authenticate with a service account restricted to the datasets you intend to expose. Cross-project queries need explicit grants.

title: Data refresh schedules
body: Refreshes run hourly on Business and every 15 minutes on Enterprise. A refresh that overruns its window is skipped rather than queued.

title: Data source credential rotation
body: Rotating a credential does not interrupt in-flight refreshes. Update the connection before the old credential is revoked.

title: Expired data source credentials
body: An expired credential fails every dependent refresh and every scheduled report that renders against it. The Delivery Log shows the underlying error.

title: Read replicas and stale reads
body: Pointing a connection at a read replica can produce reports that lag the primary. Replica lag is not surfaced in the UI.

title: Connection pool exhaustion
body: Concurrent refreshes share a pool per connection. Exhaustion appears as refresh timeouts rather than connection errors.

title: Allowlisting egress IP addresses
body: Our egress addresses are listed under Settings > Data Sources and change with at least 30 days notice.

title: CSV import size limits
body: Uploads are capped at 250 MB per file and 2 million rows. Larger datasets should be loaded through a data source connection.

title: Scheduling a CSV refresh from cloud storage
body: A storage-backed dataset can refresh on a schedule. The file must keep a stable name and schema between refreshes.

title: Schema changes in an upstream table
body: A removed or retyped column breaks dependent charts. Meridian does not migrate definitions automatically.

title: Troubleshooting slow dashboards
body: The usual cause is an unindexed join in a custom SQL block. Open the Query Profiler and look for scans over 2 million rows.

title: Query Profiler basics
body: The profiler shows per-block execution time and rows scanned. Times exclude queueing, so a fast profile can still render slowly under load.

title: Custom SQL query limits
body: Custom SQL blocks are capped at 60 seconds and 500 MB scanned on Business. Enterprise raises this to 300 seconds.

title: Caching and dashboard freshness
body: Results are cached per query for the refresh interval. A manual refresh bypasses the cache for that viewer only.

title: Dashboard filters and query pushdown
body: Filters are pushed into the query where the data source supports it. Where it does not, filtering happens after retrieval and is slower.

title: Cross-filtering between charts
body: Cross-filtering applies to charts sharing a data source. Charts on other sources are unaffected and can appear inconsistent.

title: Duplicating a dashboard
body: Duplication copies chart definitions but not schedules or alerts. Those must be recreated on the copy.

title: Dashboard load fails with a partial render
body: A partial render means one block errored while others succeeded. Each block reports its own error in place.

title: Chart type limitations
body: Some chart types require a time dimension and will refuse to render without one, rather than rendering empty.

title: Mobile dashboard rendering
body: Dashboards reflow on narrow screens. Fixed-width custom blocks may clip and are not reflowed.

title: Exporting dashboards to PDF
body: Use Share > Export > PDF. Exports over 40 pages are truncated. Scheduled PDF exports are available on Business and Enterprise.

title: Exporting chart data to CSV
body: CSV export returns the query result, not the rendered chart. Row limits match the chart's own limit.

title: Scheduled export delivery failures
body: A scheduled export shares the delivery pipeline with reports, so failures appear in the same Delivery Log.

title: Export row limits
body: Exports are capped at 1 million rows. Beyond that, query the data source directly.

title: Sharing a dashboard with a link
body: Link sharing respects row-level permissions. A recipient without access sees an empty dashboard rather than an error.

title: Embedding dashboards in your application
body: Signed embedding uses a short-lived JWT. Tokens are valid for 10 minutes and must be minted server-side; embedding keys must never ship to a browser.

title: Public dashboard links
body: Public links bypass authentication entirely and ignore row-level rules. They are disabled by default and require an owner to enable.

title: Watermarking exported files
body: Enterprise workspaces can watermark PDF exports with the viewer's identity. Watermarks are not applied to CSV.

title: API rate limits
body: The REST API allows 600 requests per minute per workspace. Exceeding it returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. Batch endpoints count as one request.

title: Handling HTTP 429 responses
body: Respect the Retry-After header and apply jitter. Retrying immediately will keep you rate limited for longer.

title: Creating and rotating API keys
body: Keys are created per service account under Settings > API. Rotation is immediate; the old key stops working on save.

title: Configuring outbound webhooks
body: Webhooks POST a JSON payload to your endpoint on alert trigger. Endpoints must return 2xx within 5 seconds or the delivery is retried three times.

title: Verifying webhook signatures
body: Each delivery carries an HMAC signature. Verify it before acting on the payload; the signing secret is shown once at creation.

title: Webhook retries and duplicate deliveries
body: Retries mean your endpoint must be idempotent. A duplicate delivery carries the same event id.

title: Pagination in list endpoints
body: List endpoints return a cursor. Cursors expire after 15 minutes and cannot be reused across parameter changes.

title: API versioning policy
body: Breaking changes ship under a new version header. Old versions are supported for 12 months after a successor is announced.

title: Slack integration setup
body: Connect Slack under Settings > Integrations. Alert delivery to a private channel requires inviting the Meridian app to that channel.

title: Programmatic report generation
body: Reports can be rendered on demand through the API. The response is asynchronous; poll the returned job id.

title: Understanding row-level permissions
body: Row-level rules filter query results per user attribute. Rules are applied at query time and cannot be bypassed by dashboard filters.

title: Inviting team members
body: Owners and Admins can invite by email. Invitations expire after 7 days. Seat count is enforced at acceptance time.

title: Role capabilities reference
body: Viewers can read, Editors can modify definitions, Admins manage users, Owners manage billing and deletion.

title: Transferring workspace ownership
body: An owner can promote another admin and step down. A workspace must always have at least one owner.

title: Group-based access control
body: Groups can be synced from your identity provider or managed locally. Local edits to a synced group are overwritten on the next sync.

title: Audit log contents and retention
body: The audit log records sign-ins, permission changes, and data source edits. Retention is 90 days on Business and 400 on Enterprise.

title: Exporting the audit log
body: Audit entries can be exported as CSV or streamed to a SIEM. Streaming is Enterprise only.

title: Data retention policy
body: Raw event data is retained for 13 months on Business and 25 months on Enterprise. Aggregates are retained indefinitely.

title: Deleting a workspace
body: Workspace deletion is soft for 30 days and recoverable by an owner. After 30 days the data is purged and cannot be restored.

title: Right to erasure requests
body: A customer record can be erased on request. Erasure is a soft delete for 30 days, then permanent, and is recorded in the audit log.

title: Data residency options
body: Enterprise workspaces can pin storage to the EU or US. Residency cannot be changed after provisioning.

title: Subprocessor list
body: Our current subprocessors are listed in the trust centre. Changes are announced 30 days in advance.

title: Support hours and SLA
body: Business plans receive a first response within one business day. Enterprise plans receive a one-hour response for Severity 1 incidents.

title: How to escalate a support ticket
body: Reply to the ticket asking for escalation, or contact your account manager. Escalation does not change the SLA clock.

title: Reporting a suspected security issue
body: Email the security address in the trust centre. Do not include credentials in the report.

title: Status page and incident history
body: Subscribe to the status page for incident notifications. Historical incidents remain visible for 12 months.

title: Renaming a workspace
body: Renaming does not change the workspace URL slug. The slug can be changed separately and old links stop working.

title: Changing your account email
body: A verification link is sent to the new address. The change applies once the link is used.

title: Downloading your data
body: An owner can request a full export. The archive is prepared asynchronously and the link expires after 7 days.

title: Browser support policy
body: The two most recent versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge are supported. Older browsers may render but are untested.

title: Keyboard shortcuts
body: Press ? on any dashboard for the shortcut list. Shortcuts are not configurable.

title: Localisation and number formats
body: Number and date formats follow the workspace locale, not the viewer's. Currency symbols are set per chart.

title: Deactivating versus deleting a user
body: Deactivation preserves the user's content and frees the seat at the next cycle. Deletion reassigns their content to an owner.

title: Trial limitations
body: Trials include Business features with a 5 seat cap and 14 day data retention. Converting preserves all content.

title: Contacting your account manager
body: Enterprise workspaces have a named account manager listed under Settings > Support.

title: Requesting a feature
body: Feature requests go through the in-app feedback form and are reviewed quarterly.

title: Sandbox workspaces
body: Enterprise plans include a sandbox workspace for testing. Sandboxes share the seat pool but not the data.

title: Migrating content between workspaces
body: Dashboards can be exported as definitions and imported elsewhere. Schedules, alerts, and permissions do not transfer.

title: Bulk user management
body: Users can be invited or deactivated in bulk from a CSV. The CSV must include the email column and may include a role column.

title: Understanding the activity feed
body: The feed shows recent edits per dashboard. It is not an audit log and omits permission changes.

title: Archiving old dashboards
body: Archived dashboards are hidden from search but keep their links working. Archiving does not stop their schedules.

title: Restoring a deleted dashboard
body: Deleted dashboards are recoverable for 30 days from the trash by an editor or above.
